newsitem.title: USA: Metra Biosystems plans workforce, cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: Metra Biosystems plans workforce, cost cuts.

text.p: Metra Biosystems Inc said on Tuesday it has begun a company-wide cost cutting plan, including work force reductions, that it expects will trim costs by 20 to 25 percent in the first quarter of 1997.

"In light of the slower than planned adoption rate for Metra and our competitors' products for bone resorption, we felt it was prudent to take these actions now," George Dunbar, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Metra Biosystems did not say how many jobs it expects to cut, and officials were immediately unavailable to comment.
The company said its plan was "to achieve profitability as soon as possible, while maintaining our long term competitive product pipeline."
Cash reserves totalled over $47 million at September 30.
Metra Biosystems' lead product for bone resorption, Pyrilinks(R)-D, was cleared for sale in the United States in December 1995.
The Company has several partnerships with companies like as Abbott Laboratories Inc, Bayer AG and Chiron Corp unit, Chiron Diagnostics.

Chiron Diagnostics recently received clearance from the FDA to market the Pyrilinks-D technology on an automated immunoassay system. Metra Biosystems said it believes this will be the first product for bone resorption to be marketed on an automated immunoassay system.
